title: Values, units and precise numeric choices

objectives.text: Calculate a notional and distinguish its stored unit from its display.
Choose an exact cent representation and reject an undeclared fractional-cent conversion.

blocks.markdown: A price of 10125 needs a declared unit. It might mean dollars, cents or exchange ticks. In this lesson prices are integer cents per share, quantities are integer shares, and notionals are cents. Do not infer the scale from the number. This simplified model excludes fees, fractional shares and sub-cent prices.

steps.text: A fill at USD 12.35 per share for 4 shares has price_cents=1235.
Multiply 1235*4=4940 cents of notional, before fees.
For nonnegative display amounts, divmod(4940,100) gives 49 dollars and 40 cents. The stored amount stays 4940 cents.

blocks.markdown:
First Python reading guide

Read the next example one line at a time. A name such as price_cents labels a value; = binds the name to the value on its right. Python * multiplies values. Text after # is a comment. print(...) displays its arguments; it does not change the stored value. divmod(notional_cents, 100) returns a pair: whole dollars and leftover cents. whole, cents = ... gives those two results separate names. In an f-string, text inside braces is replaced by a value; :02d prints an integer using at least two digits, so 6 cents displays as 06. An import line makes a library name available when a later example needs it. Predict the values before running; if Python is unavailable, trace them on paper. The functions lesson will separate returning a value from printing it.

Language references: [Python introduction](https://docs.python.org/3.12/tutorial/introduction.html) and [built-in functions](https://docs.python.org/3.12/library/functions.html). The cents/shares policy is this lesson's declared synthetic model.

blocks.source:
price_cents = 1235
quantity_shares = 4
notional_cents = price_cents * quantity_shares
whole, cents = divmod(notional_cents, 100)
print(notional_cents)
print(f"USD {whole}.{cents:02d}")
blocks.caption: Expected output: 4940, then USD 49.40. The formatting example is restricted to nonnegative amounts.

blocks.markdown: Python int stores whole numbers without a fixed 64-bit limit, but external protocols and database columns still need range checks. A float is useful for approximate calculations; it does not exactly represent many decimal fractions. Displaying two decimals does not turn an approximate value into an exact stored cent count.

blocks.source:
print(0.1 + 0.2 == 0.3)
from decimal import Decimal
print(Decimal("0.10") * 100)
blocks.caption: Expected output: False, then 10.00. Decimal starts from the text here; it also has a precision context.

blocks.markdown: If the contract accepts whole cents, input USD 12.345 is out of scope. Do not silently round. Agree a conversion rule or reject it. Some instruments legitimately use sub-cent prices; they need a different declared scale, not a claim that whole cents fit every market.

Independent transfer: price 207 cents and quantity 3 shares gives 621 cents, displayed as USD 6.21. Check the unit before converting. Later validation lessons will implement an input boundary that rejects wrong types, invalid ranges and undeclared precision.

References: [Python floating point](https://docs.python.org/3/tutorial/floatingpoint.html) and [Decimal](https://docs.python.org/3/library/decimal.html). Examples checked in Python 3.12; the exact-money model here is a deliberately bounded teaching contract.

Technical references: [Python floating-point tutorial](https://docs.python.org/3/tutorial/floatingpoint.html) for binary approximation and display; [Decimal reference](https://docs.python.org/3/library/decimal.html) for decimal construction and context. The financial schemas, policies and synthetic cases in this lesson are declared teaching contracts, not claims about a particular venue or employer.

summary: Declare units and scale. Multiply price by quantity in compatible units. Store exact whole cents when that is the contract; display formatting and arbitrary float rounding are not replacements for it.
